rows.name: 318_r108_parimana_moves
rows.source:
# R108: parimana() - one number, the bytes the program's nirmmita and kosh hold now - moving as
# allocations happen. A block gives back its nirmmita; a kosh (made inside a block or not) keeps its
# header and capacity for the program's life: kosh storage is not reclaimed yet.
mukhya() {
    likha("start ", parimana(), "\n")
    kosh k[1]
    kosh_kship(k, 1)
    likha("a kosh of 1 ", parimana(), "\n")
    kosh_kship(k, 2)
    kosh_kship(k, 3)
    likha("grown to capacity 4 ", parimana(), "\n")
    mandapa {
        vitti b = nirmmita(100)
        likha("a block's nirmmita(100) ", parimana(), "\n")
        kosh m[8]
        likha("and a kosh of 8 in it ", parimana(), "\n")
    }
    likha("after the block ", parimana(), "\n")
}
rows.expected_stdout:
start 0
a kosh of 1 48
grown to capacity 4 72
a block's nirmmita(100) 184
and a kosh of 8 in it 288
after the block 176

run.stdout:
start 0
a kosh of 1 0
grown to capacity 4 0
a block's nirmmita(100) 0
and a kosh of 8 in it 0
after the block 0

rows.name: 322_r111_new_names
rows.source:
# R111: the vocabulary change - the new names (primary from v292). Example 323 is the same program with
# the old names: both print the same and compile to the same bytes; only 323 gets the warnings.
mukhya() {
    kosh k[2]
    kosh_kship(k, 3)
    kosh_kship(k, 7)
    kosh_yuj(k, 11)
    likha("gan ", kosh_gan(k), " ksham ", kosh_ksham(k), "\n")
    likha("iksh ", kosh_iksh(k), "\n")
    likha("hri ", kosh_hri(k), "\n")
    likha("apanay ", kosh_apanay(k), "\n")
    likha("rikt ", kosh_rikt(k), "\n")
    kosh_shodh(k)
    likha("rikt ", kosh_rikt(k), "\n")
    vitti m[5]
    likha("pankti_gan ", pankti_gan(m), "\n")
    likha("laghu ", akshar_laghu(65), " guru ", akshar_guru(97), "\n")
    shabda(anka_akshar(66))
    likha_santat(42)
    likha("\n")
    vitti s = vartani_sandhi("ab", "cd")
    shabda(s)
    likha("\n")
}

rows.name: 323_r111_old_names
rows.source:
# R111: the vocabulary change - the old names, which keep working (example 322 is the same program
# with the new names). The same output and the same bytes; each old name prints one warning naming its
# replacement, on stderr, when compiled.
mukhya() {
    kosh k[2]
    kosh_push(k, 3)
    kosh_push(k, 7)
    kosh_enqueue(k, 11)
    likha("gan ", kosh_len(k), " ksham ", kosh_cap(k), "\n")
    likha("iksh ", kosh_peek(k), "\n")
    likha("hri ", kosh_pop(k), "\n")
    likha("apanay ", kosh_dequeue(k), "\n")
    likha("rikt ", kosh_empty(k), "\n")
    kosh_clear(k)
    likha("rikt ", kosh_empty(k), "\n")
    vitti m[5]
    likha("pankti_gan ", pankti_len(m), "\n")
    likha("laghu ", char_lower(65), " guru ", char_upper(97), "\n")
    shabda(char_from(66))
    lkhb(42)
    likha("\n")
    vitti s = vartani_cat("ab", "cd")
    shabda(s)
    likha("\n")
}

rows.name: 288_r86_kosh_alias_moves
rows.source:
# R86: `vitti a = k` is a second NAME for the same kosh, not a copy. Up to v283, with something allocated
# in between (obstacle), kosh_kship moved k's cells and a stayed on the old buffer (a[0]=41 k[0]=99).
# R101A (v284): on Linux every kosh has a region of its own and grows in place, so the names stay one:
# a[0]=99 k[0]=99, then a[0]=7 k[0]=7. Windows still moves (reference section 16).
mukhya() {
    kosh k[1]
    kosh_kship(k, 41)
    vitti a = k
    vitti obstacle = nirmmita(64)
    kosh_kship(k, 42)
    k[0] = 99
    likha("a[0]=", a[0], " k[0]=", k[0])
    a[0] = 7
    likha("a[0]=", a[0], " k[0]=", k[0])
}
